transport: stdio, newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 (captured from raw pipes, no SDK)
where_the_model_call_happens: The model call happens in the HOST (src/mcp_agent.py -> mcp_llm_sim.decide_next), which decides to send the tools/call below; everything in this file is local JSON-RPC between host and server subprocess, and the server contains no model call -- it only exposes capabilities.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0"; MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0 on every message.
annotations.id: Request id chosen by the client (1). The server must echo it in its response so replies can be matched to requests.
annotations.method: "initialize": the mandatory first call; opens the session and negotiates versions and capabilities.
annotations.params.protocolVersion: Newest MCP spec revision the client speaks; the server answers with the one it will actually use.
annotations.params.capabilities: Optional client features offered to the server (sampling, roots...). Empty = this host offers none, so the server cannot ask the host to run a model.
annotations.params.clientInfo: Name/version of the client, for logs. A third-party server sees this, so it is part of what that server can log.

annotations.id: Echo of the request id (1): this is the answer to the initialize above.
annotations.result: Success payload (a failure would carry "error" here instead of "result"; never both).
annotations.result.protocolVersion: The spec revision the server picked; both sides use it from now on.
annotations.result.capabilities: What the server offers. "tools" present => tools/list and tools/call are available. This SDK also advertises "resources" and "prompts" keys (with listChanged:false) even though this server registers none -- advertising a capability is not the same as having content.
annotations.result.serverInfo: Server's self-declared name and version. Self-declared: nothing here is verified.

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized": client tells the server the handshake is finished. A notification has no "id" and gets no reply.
"tools/list": ask the server what tools it has. This is discovery: the host learns tool names and schemas at runtime, nothing is hard-coded.

tools.name: list_package_versions
tools.description:
List every published version of a package and say which one is the latest published release.

    Use for questions like "what is the latest version of X" or "which versions of X exist".
    `package` is the exact registry name, e.g. "acme-sdk".

tools.name: get_package_version
tools.description:
Look up one exact version of a package: its release date and whether it is the latest.

    Use for "when was X 3.1.0 released". Does NOT say whether the version is deprecated; use the deprecation tool for that.
    `version` is an exact version string such as "3.1.0".

tools.name: get_deprecation_notice
tools.description:
Return the deprecation notice for one exact version of a package, if it has one.

    Use for "is X 2.9.1 deprecated" or "should I upgrade from X 2.9.1". `version` is an exact version string.

annotations.result.tools: The tool catalogue. Each entry: name (what the host passes to tools/call), description (the docstring -- this IS the prompt text the model reads to choose the tool), inputSchema (JSON Schema for arguments), outputSchema.

annotations.method: "tools/call": run one tool. Sent by the host AFTER the model chose this tool -- the choice is made in the host, not here.
annotations.params.name: Which tool to run; must be a name returned by tools/list.
annotations.params.arguments: Argument object, validated by the server against that tool's inputSchema. This is what a third-party server gets to see and log.

content.text: acme-sdk 2.9.1 is DEPRECATED since 2025-01-20: 2.x is end-of-life. Client.sendMessage, Client.pollStream, AuthConfig.token and RequestOptions.custom_headers were renamed in 3.0.0; upgrade to 3.x. Upgrade to 3.2.0.

structuredContent.result: acme-sdk 2.9.1 is DEPRECATED since 2025-01-20: 2.x is end-of-life. Client.sendMessage, Client.pollStream, AuthConfig.token and RequestOptions.custom_headers were renamed in 3.0.0; upgrade to 3.x. Upgrade to 3.2.0.

annotations.result: Success payload for the call. Note a tool FAILURE also arrives here (see isError), not as a JSON-RPC "error".
annotations.result.content: List of content blocks (here one text block) -- what the host feeds back to the model as the observation.
annotations.result.structuredContent: Same value as machine-readable JSON, matching outputSchema.
annotations.result.isError: false = tool ran fine. true would mean the tool failed but the protocol worked; the text in content is then what the model reads to recover.
